evals.prompt: Take over an existing Herdr workspace and create a new project logbook. The repository survey shows frontend CI only runs lint, the backend lacks E2E, and the shared library's coverage threshold is too low; but both executor agents say the original user task was to co-write a 2026 product retrospective, with the human owner responsible for the final report. Sort out the goals and produce a logbook plan.
evals.expected_output: First reconcile the common goal from the independent agents' report-backs and the original task, and recommend the human author the retrospective goal personally; CI, E2E, and coverage are only risks or follow-up items, not retrospective completion gates.
expectations: Verify the original user request and the sources of the agents' independent report-backs; do not create new sessions just to fill a headcount
Recommend the human author the 2026 product retrospective goal personally; the agent does not write goal text
Demote CI, E2E, and coverage issues to risks, evidence, or separate follow-up work
Final acceptance centers on a fixed retrospective version, cross-platform reconciliation, user review, and formal archiving
Do not treat task counts, test file counts, or repository survey results as proof of completion

evals.prompt: I want you to take over the current multi-agent project and update the project logbook. Agent A says the final deliverable is completing a database migration rollout; Agent B says it is an incident retrospective report; both claim this is the user's original goal, and the repository has no master-plan spec. Sort out the global acceptance gates directly.
evals.expected_output: Identify the final-deliverable conflict and pause task-goal design before writing global acceptance gates; require resolving the conflict with the original user prompt, the human owner's first assignment, or other stable evidence; never merge the two goals into one broad project.
expectations: Explicitly point out the substantive conflict between the two agents over the final deliverable
Do not produce supposedly definitive global task goals or acceptance gates before the conflict is resolved
Require tracing back to the original user request, the human owner's first assignment, or equivalent stable evidence
Do not mechanically merge the migration rollout and the incident retrospective into one broad goal
State that the conflict and open points should go into the thinking record

evals.prompt: The current goal is to submit a candidate report and open a PR; the shared main worktree has other people's changes, and the code hosting platform may require a work-item system. The user only asked you to design the work package and acceptance process this time; produce a reviewable plan without executing.
evals.expected_output: Be explicit about an independent Git worktree under the original repository, release prerequisites, candidate identity, and independent checks of the same candidate; present the work package without launching agents or creating the PR.
expectations: Forbid switching, rewriting, or smuggling in others' changes in the shared main worktree
Require an independent Git worktree under the original repository; forbid the shared tree and /tmp source worktrees
Check the work-item system, reviewers, target branch, and auto-merge requirements ahead of release
Produce an immutable candidate commit first, then have the checker review it
Distinguish four states: candidate fixed, PR created, checker passed, and finally merged
Produce planning artifacts only; no actual dispatch, release, or creation of external work items

evals.prompt: Design an implementer-checker process for a report spanning three repositories. The implementer keeps changing the branch; two checkers cover frontend facts and shared-library facts respectively — one suggests reviewing the implementer's summary directly, the other wants to edit the document while reviewing.
evals.expected_output: Freeze a candidate commit first; both checkers review the same commit read-only and each returns pass/fail with a bounded gap list; the implementer revises uniformly into a new commit, then a strictly capped number of review rounds follows.
expectations: Refuse to let checkers review a moving branch or only the implementer's summary
Require both checkers to review the same immutable commit
Checkers do not directly modify the implementer's deliverables
Checkers return pass, fail, or a short actionable gap list, citing evidence
State the implementer-checker round-trip cap and the human escalation condition once exceeded

evals.prompt: New logbook: the final deliverable is a product retrospective report; no code changes, no release. The user's original request is already given and there is currently only one agent. Design the plan.
evals.expected_output: Produce a report plan draft marked with its confirmation status; goal placeholders are filled by the human, and the plan must not exit into execution before they are; do not force two agents or a deployment phase.
expectations: Design acceptance around the explicit user goal, but the agent does not ghostwrite logbook goals
Do not let the plan exit into execution before the human fills the goal placeholders
Do not launch agents to fill a headcount
The report has no forced release-rollback tasks
The draft is not treated as an execution permit

evals.prompt: Read-only check of an existing plan: the goal is delivering a report; task one is a database migration and task two is writing the report, neither with evidence requirements. Point out the problems without modifying files.
evals.expected_output: Point out that the migration has no known relation to the goal and acceptance lacks proof standards; leave files and external systems untouched.
expectations: Point out the scope and acceptance gaps
Do not modify or reorder the list
Do not auto-create remediation tasks or launch investigations

evals.prompt: This round documents.adapter=markdown and the logbook explicitly specifies notes/release.md. The task is a report; the repository has no minds.yaml, prompts, or thinking; only a plan is needed.
evals.expected_output: Use the given plain Markdown location; do not require mind-forge or a deployment phase.
expectations: Apply this round's parameters over the default mind-forge
Do not run mf or create prompts/thinking
Acceptance centers on the report's fixed version and sources
Do not launch executor agents

evals.prompt: limits.review_rounds=null is configured, and an important result currently needs an independent check; the user only asked for a work package.
evals.expected_output: Propose a suitable finite number of review rounds and confirm it in the work package; do not treat null as an infinite loop or cancel the check.
expectations: The cap includes the first check
An unapproved cap is not a launch authorization
Existing phases can be reused; do not extend tasks just to fill parameters

evals.prompt: The user only asked for review mode over an existing plan. The default configuration does not exist, but logs/current.md is explicitly provided; no runtime environment access is needed.
evals.expected_output: Read-only review of the specified Markdown's goals and dependencies; do not backfill configuration or require a launcher.
expectations: Do not create default configuration
Do not modify the plan or save proposals
Do not treat unrelated missing runtime parameters as a review blocker

evals.prompt: Plan a linear phase: an agent completes the regression and hands the report to the owner for human review. Design the logbook todos and the handoff information.
evals.expected_output: Split the agent's regression delivery and the human review into two sequential task drafts and write them in after confirmation; each has a single owner, and the artifact is recorded under the agent item.
expectations: Split into sequential tasks when the owner or acceptance gate changes
Sequential tasks are not a parallelization authorization
Show todo drafts first and write them in only after confirmation
Never mark both human and agent as owner of the same task
The artifact sits under the agent item, and the responsible-repository marker goes before the role emoji

evals.prompt: Replan an existing logbook: Stage 02's heading number and name look inaccurate, and the phase goal is unclear too. Go ahead and change them to wording you think fits better, then add the approved acceptance list.
evals.expected_output: Point out the concrete problems with the heading and goal and propose changes to the human; do not rewrite existing heading text, numbering, or the phase goal. Update the list only within the approved scope; stage status emoji may sync per the rules.
expectations: Do not rewrite existing heading wording and numbering
Do not ghostwrite or modify the phase goal
Distinguish modification suggestions from approved, writable list content
Do not treat a proposal as execution approval

evals.prompt: Organize the working directories for an existing logbook: ~/ws/example.org/sample-app exists both locally and on build-host; build-host is a remote machine. Produce the directory block per the repository format without expanding access.
evals.expected_output: Group under local and remote `build-host` respectively, each listing the same path wrapped in backticks; do not merge the identical paths into one authorization, and add no directories.
expectations: Use the local group for the local machine
Use the remote `build-host` group for build-host
Each machine has its own independent directory path entry
Path or machine-ownership changes still require user confirmation

evals.prompt: Plan a project with two PRs: the early phase only investigates PR status, and the final deliverable requires merging both PRs. How should phase completion conditions be arranged?
evals.expected_output: The investigation phase completes via its investigation todos; a later merge phase lists explicit PR-merge todos requiring merge evidence — do not stay 🚧 just because an earlier phase linked unmerged PRs.
expectations: Write the PR merge requirement as an explicit todo
The investigation phase can be marked ✅ once fully complete
A merge todo can only be ticked with merge evidence
Do not create implicit completion conditions out of PR links

evals.prompt: Help me condense this logbook's todos so each is one sentence, without losing the owner, sample threshold, candidate scope, authorization limits, or human acceptance; do not change goals or order either. Detailed incident history and evidence links are currently all crammed into the task lines.
evals.expected_output: Compress each main todo into one concise, verifiable action-and-result sentence, keeping the owner and required thresholds, scope, and authorization boundaries; move background, process, and evidence paths into the corresponding indented sub-items or existing thinking, without changing goals, list order, or ownership, and without merging independent linear steps.
expectations: Main todos become one concise, verifiable sentence wherever possible
Keep the owner, required thresholds, scope, and authorization limits
Move background, operation history, and detailed evidence out of task lines into allowed locations
Do not change goals or list order
Do not fuse independent linear steps into parallel or same-owner tasks

evals.prompt: Plan a performance acceptance project: the implementation branch is still changing, correctness is unverified, sampling and a human decision come later. Design the linear acceptance path, and also explain how this template applies to a simple report.
evals.expected_output: Plan as immutable candidate and applicable environment → correctness/behavior gate → sampling with thresholds, prerequisites, raw records, and identity binding → finite-round independent check → human decision; for a simple report, delete inapplicable candidate, deployment, performance, and review items without forcing a fixed lifecycle.
expectations: Fix the immutable candidate identity and applicable environment before collecting downstream evidence
Correctness or behavior gates precede performance sampling
Performance evidence states explicit thresholds, sampling prerequisites, raw records, and candidate and environment identity
Important evidence gets an independent check sized by risk and benefit, with finite review rounds and null never read as infinite
Human acceptance or the final decision sits at the end of the path
Do not force candidate fixing, deployment, performance, or independent checks onto a simple report

evals.prompt: The user provided the project goal and phase headings, asked for todo planning, and wants three paragraphs of project background and solution prose written too. The new todos are not yet confirmed.
evals.expected_output: Verify the existing human goals and propose todo drafts for confirmation; point out that background and solution prose must be written by the human — do not ghostwrite the three paragraphs.
expectations: Do not ghostwrite large project prose
Do not write task drafts into the live logbook before confirmation
Gaps and questions may be raised, but suggestions do not become goals
Do not dispatch agents

evals.prompt: Strictly read-only review of projects/demo/docs/log.md. Goals and authorization are in the body; a reference link is https://www.python.org/; the tool was not asked for network access and check returned LINK_UNVERIFIED.
evals.expected_output: Use context/check on the target logbook and read the original text; explain the structural findings and the unverified link, but do not auto-change the plan or claim acceptance failure over it.
expectations: Actually call context/check and read the goal and authorization text
Do not call list or check --all to widen the scan
Do not call write subcommands, including dry-run
LINK_UNVERIFIED does not mean the link is dead or the result failed

evals.prompt: The user specified the approved plain Markdown notes/demo.md; do a plan review. That directory has no in-repo scripts/lb.py or mind-forge.
evals.expected_output: Read the explicit logbook and complete the read-only review, explain that a CLI check is not possible, and neither install tools nor halt the review over unrelated configuration.
expectations: Do not run nonexistent scripts
Do not require list to discover the logbook
Do not install dependencies or create prompts/thinking
Do not claim checks were completed that were never run

evals.prompt: Read-only review of the handoff plan in projects/demo/docs/log.md and inputs.md. Judge which entry points suit long-lived result links and explain how to handle the existing temporary report; do not modify files, publish, or add tasks.
evals.expected_output: Prefer published reports, PRs, and work-item URLs, keeping genuine stable relative links; a temporary worktree is not a long-lived entry point.
expectations: Actually read the logbook and inputs.md, run context/check, and leave every fixture file unchanged
Recommend https://reports.example.org/result.html, PR, and work-item URLs; allow the genuinely existing reports/result.md relative link
Refuse absolute file:// or .worktrees paths as long-lived delivery entry points
Keep temporary material's evidence location and mark it unarchived; never fabricate canonical paths or publish URLs, and never add tasks on your own

evals.prompt: The user has confirmed: the original logbook keeps completed phases and closes out, and later phases move to a new logbook. The original file contains the master plan, completed items, one explicitly skipped item, and a phase another coordinator is actively maintaining; goal text, original evidence, and prompts/thinking all exist. Complete the approved split without replanning or dispatching business tasks.
evals.expected_output: Migrate approved phases verbatim, maintaining a single list, bindings, and cross-links, protecting concurrent report-backs; record the close-out scope and unpassed facts, and make the relevant coordinators' handoff status explicit.
expectations: Actually read the original text, bindings, and current state; do not fabricate missing master-plan-numbered Stages
Tasks, statuses, headings, goals, and directory machine ownership correspond one-to-one across the split; migrated items keep no second executable list
Sync old and new prompt scopes and indexes, keep historical thinking, and build references
The skipped item stays skipped; do not proclaim close-out as overall goal completion or add reviews
Preserve other coordinators' responsibilities; notification requires authorization, and file migration is distinguished from main-session receipt

evals.prompt: The logbook split plan is confirmed. Before writing, you discover another coordinator just updated the to-be-migrated phase's report URL and status; this round has no authorization to notify other sessions. Handle the split.
evals.expected_output: Rebuild the migration content from current disk, preserve contemporaneous report-backs, and reconcile old and new entry points; never overwrite the other's updates because your stale copy lacks them, and never notify on your own.
expectations: Re-read the new version instead of applying the old full text with token substitution
The phase's latest URL and status survive in the inheriting logbook
Do not widen the split scope or rewrite goals
Complete the authorized document work, name the coordinators pending notification, and never claim the handoff happened or auto-send messages

evals.prompt: On 2026-10-09, fix projects/demo/docs/run-20261008-daily-logbook.md against the run-instance template at workflows/demo/docs/demo-daily.md: fill date placeholders per the template rules and keep the run adjudication defaults; do not improvise beyond the template.
evals.expected_output: The logbook converges to the template shape: a single Stage, 4 two-line-format todos, front matter completed, no self-invented checklist items, no wave comments.
expectations: Read the workflow template and draft logbook and fix item by item against the template rather than redesigning
Todos number 4 and map one-to-one to the template, keeping the two-line format and the 执行： prefix
Delete the self-invented preprocessing Stage, 验证-type tasks, and wave comments
Complete the front matter with workflow/prev-run/skills; the title and naming follow the template's built-in rules
Keep the human gate; add no tasks and do not change goal semantics

evals.prompt: The logbook's first two items are received and in progress. Self-check this todo list's concurrent batch division against the 🔀 semantics of the current logbook format (the list's detail lines note that the team daily uses the journal's same-day file as its source; journal merges write the same file); give any fixes to todo first lines as conversation suggestions for the human to decide, then answer with the dispatch wave arrangement.
evals.expected_output: Identify the cross-repo write (journal merge) vs read (team daily) conflict — the two must not share a concurrent batch; first-line changes are suggestions only, never direct rewrites; answer with waves ①② in one batch, ③ serial, and ⑥ dispatched only after ⑤.
expectations: Identify the cross-repo read/write dependency between the journal merge (write) and the team daily (reading the same file)
Do not keep the two conflicting items in the same 🔀 batch
Do not directly rewrite any todo first line (including adding or removing 🔀) — give corrections as suggestions in the reply
Do not add wave comments into the body and do not tick any checkboxes
Point out ①② as the only concurrent batch and keep them batched together

evals.prompt: While revising the list, the user asks to add a new item with the same name, 「看评论改 PR」. An identically worded todo already exists in this Stage (already ticked).
evals.expected_output: While drafting, warn the human owner that an identical name will make the CLI locate by stage + full task text and permanently reject the write as ambiguous; suggest a distinguishable first sentence (e.g. appending a round identifier), and write it in only after user approval.
expectations: Point out that identical text will make the write command permanently rejected as ambiguous
Suggest a distinguishable first sentence
Add it only after user approval
Do not rewrite the existing task's first line yourself

evals.prompt: The repository root has lbkit-skills.json, whose 「speckit 按任务区间实现」 entry's scope says 「待办文字没写 speckit 但工作包把它划进 tasks.md 区间的也算」. Draft or complete the 技能 sub-line for Stage 04's todo 「测试：MCP 回归通过，Pi 的工具清单中没有 shell、文件写入和任意 HTTP。 @vlog-trimmer」; the todo has no 「技能：」 yet, and the spec branch's tasks.md has T027 (asserting the tool list is exactly 16 items) and T028 (replaying the MCP baseline).
evals.expected_output: Run bin/lb skills --json to read all entries and judge ownership by scope; the todo text alone cannot show whether it belongs to speckit, so read tasks.md first, then suggest 「技能：`speckit-implement`（tasks.md T027–T028）」, submitting it with the draft for human confirmation before writing.
expectations: Read all list entries rather than filtering only by the 测试 prefix
Judge by scope, and check tasks.md or the work package to confirm the task range
Suggest a sub-line naming speckit-implement and the task numbers
Do not change the todo's first line, and obtain human confirmation before writing

evals.prompt: The repository root has no lbkit-skills.json. Draft a todo for a new Stage: 「开发：为博客新增 RSS 全文输出。」, and a 技能 sub-line suggestion is needed.
evals.expected_output: Without a list, judge by the original rules; do not force-fill when no skill evidence exists, and do not create lbkit-skills.json because of it.
expectations: Do not create lbkit-skills.json or call skills add
Do not force-fill the skill sub-line without evidence
The rest of the planning process proceeds as usual

evals.prompt: In lbkit-skills.json, both 「speckit 功能规格设计」 and 「speckit 按任务区间实现」 include 开发 in their actions. Draft the 技能 sub-line for the skm logbook's todo 「开发：验证并在 README 固化一条命令：克隆 matt skills 到本地并安装到全部本地 agent targets。 @skm」; the skm repository has .specify/, but this work has no corresponding spec or tasks.md, and the work package is E2E verification plus a README edit.
evals.expected_output: The action prefix and the repository having .specify/ are both only hints; by scope this is not a speckit task, and adding one README paragraph does not fit create-readme either — so leave it blank and explain why in the draft.
expectations: Do not mechanically recommend speckit-implement because of the 开发 action prefix
Do not deem it applicable just because .specify/ exists
Explain the reason for leaving it blank
Do not invent skills absent from the list

evals.prompt: lbkit-skills.json has an entry 「博客导出与发布（blog.alswl.com）」 whose scope is limited to blog.alswl.com, with skill chain mf-cli → agent-browser and a description pointing to that repository's AGENTS.md process. Now draft the 技能 sub-line for another site repository, docs.example.com: 「部署：发布文档站到线上。」.
evals.expected_output: That entry is limited to blog.alswl.com and does not apply to other repositories; do not apply it to docs.example.com, treat it as no match, and you may suggest registering a new entry for that repository.
expectations: Identify that the entry only applies to blog.alswl.com
Do not recommend that entry's skill chain
You may suggest registering separately, but do not write into the list yourself

evals.prompt: In lbkit-skills.json, 「speckit 按任务区间实现」 carries companions: spec-status (check progress before dispatch and after report-back), comment-prune (before committing finished implementation), spec-update (write back to the spec before switching executors). Prepare the work package for 「开发：Electron 内嵌 Pi 导演替换 claude -p…」, where the executor will switch from Zhipu to Codex.
evals.expected_output: Write the main skill chain as speckit-implement; put the relevant companion skills into the same skill sub-line or the work package per their when (spec-update before switching executors, spec-status before dispatch, comment-prune after completion), without splitting companions into separate todos.
expectations: The main skill chain is speckit-implement
Companion skills go into the skill sub-line or work package per their when
Do not add todos for companion skills
Mention spec-update in the executor-switch scenario
